recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If the work group wants MeasureReport.supplementalData to carry linkId/code/id categorization directly, handle that as a new substantive modeling issue rather than a FHIR-25718 reconciliation fix.
issue_request: FHIR-25718 was a Published/Persuasive R5 CQI change request asking to restore guidance that identifiers coordinate MeasureReport results with corresponding Measure population, stratifier, and supplementalData definitions after R4 removed the STU3 identifier elements and relied on Element.id.
initial_application: The Jira comments identify e9e025abe745570e34e38009ffafc2570c0bb4a9 and HL7/fhir#2879 as the application. That commit updated source/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html with linking-id guidance; by then FHIR-38832 had introduced linkId as the current R5 correlation mechanism, so the applied text used linkId rather than newly recommending Element.id.
additional_context: Measure and MeasureReport are active resources. FHIR-38832 added linkId and already has a combined-branch audit; FHIR-49670 later clarified MeasureReport correspondence and already has a combined-branch audit; FHIR-37559 established MeasureReport.supplementalData as Reference(Resource); and FHIR-50012 removed the stale supplementalData linkId wording from the quality-reporting page while preserving group/population/stratifier linkId guidance. A 2025 Zulip implementer question identifies possible future supplementalData categorization work, but it is not a final source-change decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already preserves the issue's implementer-facing guidance through linkId definitions and narrative, plus backwards-compatible id comments. Re-adding supplementalData to the MeasureReport linkId paragraph would be inaccurate because MeasureReport.supplementalData is a reference and supplementalData reporting is documented through references and contained Observations.
